criteria.description: `/` is a public marketing landing page with product story, a clear primary CTA, and a Login with GitHub action; it renders with no session and exposes no dashboard data or actions
verification: Open `/` in a fresh browser with no session cookie
Expect HTTP 200 and page renders without redirect
Page shows product/story copy, one prominent primary CTA, and a visible “Login with GitHub” control
No release, operation, or repository data from any account is shown
Clicking “Login with GitHub” leads to the GitHub OAuth flow (`/auth/github` or `/login`)

criteria.description: An authenticated user visiting `/` still sees the marketing page (no redirect) with the primary CTA changed to “Go to dashboard” linking to `/dashboard`
verification: Complete GitHub OAuth using the deterministic fake so a session exists
Navigate to `/`
Expect HTTP 200, the marketing page renders, no redirect occurs
The primary CTA reads “Go to dashboard” and navigates to `/dashboard` when clicked

criteria.description: Unauthenticated access to any `/dashboard` route redirects to `/login` and renders no dashboard data or actions
verification: With no session, request `/dashboard`, `/dashboard/releases`, `/dashboard/operations`, `/dashboard/settings/github`, `/dashboard/settings/schedule`
Each ends on `/login` (redirect)
No dashboard data or action controls are rendered on the way
A protected API route (e.g. releases list) still returns 401 without a session

criteria.description: `/login` is a dedicated sign-in page whose GitHub button starts OAuth, and completing OAuth lands the user on `/dashboard`
verification: Open `/login` with no session; expect 200 and an editorial sign-in layout with a GitHub button
Click the button and complete OAuth with the deterministic fake
Final location is `/dashboard` (not `/settings/github` or `/`)
The dashboard renders as an authenticated view

criteria.description: The authenticated dashboard uses a responsive left sidebar (not top navigation) with section links plus sign-out, and the logo links to `/`
verification: Authenticate and open `/dashboard` at a desktop viewport (≥1200px)
A left sidebar is present with links to Overview, Releases, Operations, GitHub, Schedule, and a sign-out control; there is no top navigation bar
Each link navigates to the matching `/dashboard/...` route and marks itself active
Clicking the Release Manager logo/wordmark navigates to `/`
Resize to a narrow viewport (≤600px): the sidebar collapses to a toggle control that opens and closes it

criteria.description: A gold accent is visibly present in the authenticated app and the design context is documented in `.impeccable.md`
verification: Inspect `/dashboard`: a gold accent color is applied to primary actions and/or the active nav item
`.impeccable.md` exists at the release-manager repo root and documents audience, typography pairing, neumorphic tokens, the gold accent token, and accessibility rules
Primary text/background combinations meet WCAG AA contrast (spot-check headings and body with a contrast checker)

criteria.description: Existing release workflow behavior is preserved through the redesigned UI
verification: Authenticate and connect a repository via `/dashboard/settings/github` using the deterministic GitHub fake
On `/dashboard`, trigger “Scan now”
A draft release appears under `/dashboard/releases`; open it at `/dashboard/releases/{id}`
Attempt approval without an actor/reason and confirm it is rejected; provide actor + reason and confirm publication is attempted
Navigation and refresh alone start no scan

criteria.description: The full deterministic verification suite passes
verification: Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` — all pass
Run `npm --prefix frontend test` — all pass
Run `npm --prefix frontend run test:e2e` — all pass, including tests for the auth gate, post-login landing on `/dashboard`, sidebar, and logo-to-`/` link
Run `npm --prefix frontend run build` — succeeds

note: The definition of done. Later phases may ONLY flip `passes`. Editing or removing a criterion is a gate failure.
